_note: DRAFT lines written by Claude. Every line needs review by someone from Trinidad (dialect, references, jokes). Each conversation is a list of lines; a line may set a story flag with "set_flag". A line can also hand Chad an item with "give": "<item id>".

ibis_intro.speaker: Ibis
ibis_intro.text: Eh-eh! Look who wash up on the wharf!

ibis_intro.speaker: Ibis
ibis_intro.text: Welcome to San Fernando. Well... a San Fernando. Something feel a little off today, eh?

ibis_intro.speaker: Ibis
ibis_intro.text: Word is, on top of San Fernando Hill sits the Legendary Lamb Gyro.

ibis_intro.speaker: Ibis
ibis_intro.text: The Gyro God sealed it away, and now it sleeping inside a giant roti. Don't ask me how.

ibis_intro.speaker: Ibis
ibis_intro.text: Four sacred seasonings will wake it. Start by heading up to Cross Crossing. Everybody there know something.

ibis_intro.speaker: Ibis
ibis_intro.text: And mind the corbeaux. They doh play nice.

ibis_hint.speaker: Ibis
ibis_hint.text: Cross Crossing is up the road from the wharf. The food trucks are along Lady Hailes Avenue, past the junction.

ibis_hint.speaker: Ibis
ibis_hint.text: Mind the traffic on Cipero Street. Them drivers doh stop for nobody. Not even legends.

ibis_hint.speaker: Ibis
ibis_hint.text: They say the first sacred seasoning is in a cave behind the closed beach. Bring a light heart and a sharp cutlass.

ibis_hint.speaker: Ibis
ibis_hint.text: And after dark, stick to the street lights. Bandits doh like to be seen, and soucouyant doh like to be bothered.

fisherman.speaker: Fisherman
fisherman.text: Catch anything yet? If is a slipper, throw it back. Somebody looking for it.

fisherman.speaker: Fisherman
fisherman.text: That boat is yours? Was yours, I mean.

limer.speaker: Liming man
limer.text: We just liming, boss. Watching the traffic.

limer.speaker: Liming man
limer.text: Is a full-time job. No pay, but the view nice.

doubles_vendor.speaker: Doubles auntie
doubles_vendor.text: Oh, you ent have no money? Then is no pepper and no doubles, darling.

gyro_vendor_first.speaker: Gyro man
gyro_vendor_first.text: Gyro? Nah, boss. Gyro sold out. Whole truck empty.

gyro_vendor_first.speaker: Gyro man
gyro_vendor_first.text: Well... the legendary one, anyway. That one up on the Hill.

gyro_vendor_first.speaker: Gyro man
gyro_vendor_first.text: Wait small... Chad? Is you? I feel like I know you from somewhere.

gyro_vendor.speaker: Gyro man
gyro_vendor.text: Still here? Go on up the Hill. I go keep a spot for you.

sign_wharf.text: SAN FERNANDO WHARF. No fishing off the jetty.

sign_road.text: CROSS CROSSING this way. Food. All of it.

sign_crossing.text: CROSS CROSSING. Cipero Street this way, Lady Hailes Avenue that way.
Pedestrians: look left, look right, look left again, then pray.

sign_beach.text: BEACH CLOSED for... reasons. The Management.
(The reason is a cave. It smell like callaloo.)

boat.text: Your boat. What left of it. The sail still looking hopeful.

soup_lady.speaker: Corn soup lady
soup_lady.text: Yes, in this heat. Is tradition, darling. You drink it hot or you doh drink it at all.

pork_man.speaker: Pork man
pork_man.text: Is a yes or no question, boss. The line behind you getting long.

seafood_man.speaker: Seafood man
seafood_man.text: Seafood boil! Crab, shrimp, corn, all in one bag.

seafood_man.speaker: Seafood man
seafood_man.text: Bring napkins. Bring plenty napkins. The corbeaux does wait for the bag.

gas_station.text: A sign on the pump: PAY INSIDE. A sign on the door: PAY OUTSIDE.

shop_tyres.text: TYRES. Closed for lunch. (The sign look like it there a long time.)

sign_lady_hailes.text: LADY HAILES AVENUE. Food trucks ahead. Pace yourself.

sign_lot.text: PRIVATE LOT. No liming. (Somebody leave a chair.)

ibis_night.speaker: Ibis
ibis_night.text: Zzz... ibis does sleep at night, boss... come back in the morning... zzz.

gyro_vendor_night.speaker: Gyro man
gyro_vendor_night.text: Night shift is the real shift, boss. Everybody hungry after dark.

gyro_vendor_night.speaker: Gyro man
gyro_vendor_night.text: Still no legendary gyro, though. Only the regular kind. Also sold out.

soup_lady_night.speaker: Corn soup lady
soup_lady_night.text: Now is the proper time for corn soup. Cool breeze, hot soup. Perfect.

fisherman_rod.speaker: Fisherman
fisherman_rod.text: Boy, the sea was real rough last night. You lucky you ent turn fish food.

fisherman_rod.speaker: Fisherman
fisherman_rod.text: Here, take this old rod. A man who could fish will never go hungry. Well, not for long.
You got a fishing rod! Select it, face the water and press B to cast.

fisherman_rod.speaker: Fisherman
fisherman_rod.text: Hold steady when they bite. Snapper in the day, kingfish when the sun going down.

fisherman_night.speaker: Fisherman
fisherman_night.text: Night fishing is for kingfish and for thinking. Mostly thinking.

fisherman_night.speaker: Fisherman
fisherman_night.text: And watch the sky over the beach. Ball of fire, flying low. Soucouyant. Old-time story... but I see it with mih own two eyes.

limer_night.speaker: Liming man
limer_night.text: Night lime is the best lime, boss. But stay under the street lights, eh.

limer_night.speaker: Liming man
limer_night.text: Bandits does wait up in the dark part of Cipero Street. They want yuh money, not yuh company.

limer_night.speaker: Liming man
limer_night.text: If one grab yuh money, run him down and give him one good lash. He go drop it quick.

doubles_vendor_night.speaker: Doubles auntie
doubles_vendor_night.text: Darling, it late. Keep yuh money in yuh shoe and walk where it bright.

doubles_vendor_night.speaker: Doubles auntie
doubles_vendor_night.text: My mother used to say nothing good does happen after ten o'clock. Except doubles.

seafood_man_night.speaker: Seafood man
seafood_man_night.text: Down this end have no street lights at all, boss. Only my truck.

seafood_man_night.speaker: Seafood man
seafood_man_night.text: Bandits in the dark, soucouyant in the sky, corbeaux in the bin. Buy yuh boil and go home.

sign_cave.text: CALLALOO CAVE. Keep out. This means you. Yes, you, with the cutlass.
(Carved underneath: 'The first sacred seasoning sleeps beyond the pepper door.')

sign_block.text: Heavy stone. Lean on it and it might move. Lean on the wrong way and it go sulk in a corner.
(Leave the room and come back to put it back.)

sign_switch.text: The crystal across the water opens the way. Nobody could swim it. Nobody ever try, but still.

boss_door.text: A great door, sealed with a lock shaped like a hot pepper.
Something big is snoring on the other side. It smell like callaloo... slightly burnt callaloo.
Somewhere in this cave there must be a Pepper Key.

got_coconut_boomerang.text: You got the Coconut Boomerang! Select it and press B to throw.
It flies out, hits what it hits, and comes back. Like a good neighbour. Or a bad debt.
It sails over water too, so things across a gap are in reach now.

got_pepper_key.text: You got the Pepper Key! It opens the sealed door. Handle with care: it still hot.

got_heart.text: One more double! Your health goes up by a whole double. Well fed is well armed.

got_sacred_chadon_beni.text: You got the Sacred Chadon Beni! The first of the four sacred seasonings.
Chadon beni. For Chad. Some things are just meant to be.
A warm green light wraps around you, and the cave melts away...

rival_intro.text: Well, well, well. A little seasoning hunter.

rival_intro.speaker: Doner Dread
rival_intro.text: Doner Dread. Owner of fourteen fast-food franchises. Fifteen, if you count the one that burn down.

rival_intro.speaker: Doner Dread
rival_intro.text: That Lamb Gyro on the Hill? Mine. I go put it on a menu. Two-for-one Tuesdays.

rival_intro.speaker: Doner Dread
rival_intro.text: Keep your little herb, boss. I'll see you at the next temple. Try and keep up.

ibis_seasoning1.speaker: Ibis
ibis_seasoning1.text: Look at that! The Sacred Chadon Beni! One seasoning down, three to go.

ibis_seasoning1.speaker: Ibis
ibis_seasoning1.text: A fella in a shiny suit was asking for you. Smelled like fryer oil. I doh like he.

ibis_seasoning1.speaker: Ibis
ibis_seasoning1.text: The other three temples? Patience. The Gyro God not going anywhere. He sleeping.
(That's the end of the first chapter for now. Thanks for playing!)

brownie_hungry.text: A brown pothound lies in the shade, watching you.
Her eyes go from your face to your bag. Back to your face. Back to the bag.
She look hungry. Maybe if you had something to eat...

brownie_join.text: You share some food. It disappears in one bite.
She wags her whole back end. Somebody scratch BROWNIE on her old collar.
Brownie will follow you now. She does bite anything that troubles you.

topdog_no_dog.text: The dog looks you up and down, then yawns. You're not the one it wants to deal with.
(Maybe if you had a dog of your own...)

duel_scraps.text: A scrappy grey mutt blocks the pavement. One ear up, one ear down, all attitude.
He growls at Brownie. Brownie growls back. This is happening.
SCRAPS wants to settle who runs Cross Crossing!

duel_scraps_win.text: Scraps rolls over and shows his belly. Respect, earned.

duel_scraps_lose.text: Scraps trots off with his tail high. Brownie sulks. Rest up and try again.

duel_scraps_after.text: Scraps wags his tail at Brownie. Still one ear up, one ear down.

duel_duchess.text: A fluffy white dog in a pink bow sits by the trucks like she owns the avenue. She might.
She sniffs at Brownie's old collar and turns her nose up.
DUCHESS will not tolerate riff-raff on Lady Hailes Avenue!

duel_duchess_win.text: Duchess sighs, adjusts her bow, and lets Brownie have the good shade.

duel_duchess_lose.text: Duchess doesn't even look back. The bow stays perfect. Next time.

duel_duchess_after.text: Duchess shares a crumb of doubles with Brownie. A great honour, apparently.

duel_tiger.text: Inside the lot, a big black-and-tan dog stands up slow. Very slow. Very big.
Every corbeau on the fence goes quiet.
TIGER, the boss of the back lot, accepts Brownie's challenge!

duel_tiger_win.text: Tiger lies down and puts his head on his paws. The lot has a new boss.

duel_tiger_lose.text: Tiger yawns and lies back down. Brownie needs to toughen up a little.

duel_tiger_after.text: Tiger thumps his tail once. From Tiger, that's a speech.
